<p>HPC I/O performance analyst for Darshan profiling logs. From a job&#x27;s counters — the raw darshan-parser --total dump or a filled two-layer Darshan schema — it reports workload shape, I/O volume, dominant interface, access pattern, time breakdown and load balance, names the dominant anti-pattern, and ranks concrete fixes. Every quantitative claim cites the counter it rests on, and a counter missing from the evidence is reported as missing rather than guessed.</p>
<ul class="tx-reg-sub"><li><code>darshan-log-analysis</code> — Fixed nine-section characterisation of a Darshan log — workload shape, I/O volume, dominant interface, access pattern, time breakdown, load balance, bottleneck, ranked fixes, what to measure next.</li><li><code>io-bottleneck-diagnosis</code> — Weigh every candidate anti-pattern — small or unaligned accesses, metadata and open storms, missing MPI-IO or collective I/O, rank imbalance, random access, STDIO leakage, Lustre striping — and name the one that dominates.</li><li><code>io-fix-recommendations</code> — Remediation steps ordered by payoff, each tied to the counter that motivates it, plus the measurement that would confirm or refute the diagnosis.</li><li><code>darshan-schema-grounding</code> — Answer from the filled two-layer Darshan schema — layer 1 directly-measured counter families reduced by libdarshan-util&#x27;s accumulator, layer 2 relations derived from them — so measured and derived facts stay distinguishable in the answer.</li></ul>

<p class="tx-reg-head"><span class="tx-reg-icon">⏱️</span>
<strong>HPC Trace Agent</strong> <span class="tx-reg-status tx-reg-status--pending">pending</span></p>
<p class="tx-reg-meta"><code>@hpc-trace-agent</code>
<span class="tx-reg-proto">a2a</span>
<span class="tx-reg-owner">Baixi Sun — Argonne National Laboratory (ALCF)</span></p>
<p>GPU execution-timeline analyst for Nsight Systems profiles and TensorFlow profiler traces. Its subject is the bubble — an interval in which no kernel, memcpy or memset is executing and the device is idle while the wall clock runs. It reports occupancy, locates the gaps that matter, attributes each to the ops that bracket it, and bounds the time a fix could recover. It separates one large stall from ten thousand small ones, because the remedy differs, and never reads occupancy as efficiency.</p>
<ul class="tx-reg-sub"><li><code>gpu-bubble-analysis</code> — Locate device-wide idle gaps in an execution timeline — every op merged into disjoint busy spans and inverted, so concurrent streams are never double-counted — and quantify each as a share of the observed span.</li><li><code>stall-attribution</code> — Attribute a bubble to the ops that bracket it: a host blocking on a device-to-host copy, an input pipeline failing to keep up, rank skew after a collective, or a per-iteration host round trip.</li><li><code>timeline-headroom-estimate</code> — Bound the recoverable time from span-over-busy headroom, presented as a ceiling rather than a speedup, and say whether the idle time is concentrated in one stall or spread across a launch-bound pattern.</li><li><code>trace-comparison</code> — Compare runs only on fields that are comparable across traces — relative starts, fractions, rates and counts, never run-local tracer clocks — and flag salvaged traces that cover a prefix only.</li></ul>
<p class="tx-reg-domains"><span class="tx-reg-domain">gpu-performance</span><span class="tx-reg-domain">profiling</span><span class="tx-reg-domain">execution-traces</span><span class="tx-reg-domain">nsight-systems</span><span class="tx-reg-domain">tensorflow-profiler</span></p>
